classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two brands' unit prices for two specified volumes and round monetary results to the nearest cent.

content.prompt: Brand A of fruit juice is priced at $\$4.50$ for a bottle containing 1000 millilitres = 1 litre of juice. Brand B of juice costs $\$4.00$ for a bottle containing 750 millilitres of the same type of juice. Calculate the unit price (rounding correct to the nearest cent) using:

children.label: a
children.prompt: the price of each per 50 millilitres

answer.short: Brand A: 23 cents per 50 mL; Brand B: 27 cents per 50 mL.
answer.worked:
Brand A has $1000\div50=20$ portions of 50 mL.

$$\begin{align*}\text{A's cost per 50 mL}&=\$4.50\div20\\\text{A's cost per 50 mL}&=\$0.225\\\text{A's cost per 50 mL}&\approx\$0.23\end{align*}$$

Brand B has $750\div50=15$ portions of 50 mL.

$$\begin{align*}\text{B's cost per 50 mL}&=\$4.00\div15\\\text{B's cost per 50 mL}&=\$\frac{4}{15}\\\text{B's cost per 50 mL}&\approx\$0.27\end{align*}$$

The prices are 23 cents and 27 cents per 50 mL, respectively, to the nearest cent.

children.label: b
children.prompt: the price of each per 100 millilitres

answer.short: Brand A: 45 cents per 100 mL; Brand B: 53 cents per 100 mL.
answer.worked:
Brand A has $1000\div100=10$ portions of 100 mL.

$$\begin{align*}\text{A's cost per 100 mL}&=\$4.50\div10\\\text{A's cost per 100 mL}&=\$0.45\end{align*}$$

Brand B has $750\div100=7.5$ portions of 100 mL.

$$\begin{align*}\text{B's cost per 100 mL}&=\$4.00\div7.5\\\text{B's cost per 100 mL}&=\$\frac{8}{15}\\\text{B's cost per 100 mL}&\approx\$0.53\end{align*}$$

The prices are 45 cents and 53 cents per 100 mL, respectively, to the nearest cent. Use the original bottle prices rather than doubling the rounded answers from part a.
